titleText.es: Apple aplica licor por goteo intravenoso.
titleText.noteEn: The title text extends the joke by imagining that Apple controls programmers' alcohol level with an automated intravenous drip.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: as (introducing a name or label)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After words such as conocido, llamado, or descrito, unaccented como introduces the name, title, or label by which something is known.

example.es: Es conocido como el padre de la medicina.
example.en: He is known as the father of medicine.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: do you remember?; you remember (formal singular)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Recuerda can be either an informal command, “remember,” or the ordinary present form for él, ella, or formal usted. A question addressed formally selects the present-tense “do you remember?” reading.

example.es: Señora, ¿recuerda este lugar?
example.en: Ma'am, do you remember this place?

cardDefinitions.answerEn: ability; capacity
alcohol
blood
peak; highest point
discovered (masculine singular)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Descubierto is the irregular completed-action form of descubrir, “to discover”; Spanish does not use the expected form descubrido. In a passive description it changes to match what was discovered: descubierto, descubierta, descubiertos, or descubiertas.

example.es: La isla fue descubierta por una exploradora.
example.en: The island was discovered by an explorer.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a finales de, “in the late part of”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The preposition a is required in the time expression a finales de. Natural English normally renders the full expression with “in,” not by translating a alone.

example.es: Llegaron a finales de junio.
example.en: They arrived in late June.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: late part; end (in a finales de)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Final means “end.” Its plural form finales is used in a finales de to locate something near the end of a month, year, decade, or other period.

example.es: La tienda abrió a finales de verano.
example.en: The store opened in late summer.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; introduces the period after a finales de
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In a finales de, de connects the expression to the period whose late part is meant. English normally folds the whole expression into “in late…” rather than translating de separately.

example.es: Volveremos a finales de mayo.
example.en: We will return in late May.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: unknown (feminine singular)
no separate English word; begins de alguna manera, “somehow”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De is fixed in de alguna manera. Translate the three words together as “somehow” or “in some way,” rather than translating de on its own.

example.es: De alguna manera, encontró la salida.
example.en: Somehow, she found the exit.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: grants; confers
superhuman (feminine singular)
effect
delicate; sensitive (masculine singular)
requires
calibration; careful adjustment to a standard
careful (feminine singular)
to give them; to give to the group
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Darle joins dar, the dictionary form meaning “to give,” to le, a small recipient word. The recipient may also be named later with a, as in darle el libro a Marta. A group can still take singular le because the noun grupo is singular.

example.es: Voy a darle la llave a Marta.
example.en: I am going to give Marta the key.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins sin más, “just like that”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sin normally means “without,” but sin más functions as a fixed expression for doing something with no further thought, preparation, explanation, or ceremony.

example.es: No puedes entrar sin más.
example.en: You cannot just walk in like that.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; completes sin más, “just like that”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Más usually means “more,” but in the fixed expression sin más it suggests that nothing further is added: no extra thought, preparation, explanation, or ceremony.

example.es: Se marchó sin más.
example.en: He simply left without another word.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: supply; stock provided for use
whisky; whiskey
for (enough or intended to cover a period of time)
programmers (masculine or mixed group)
to tell them; to say to them
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Decirles joins decir, the dictionary form meaning “to say” or “to tell,” to les, which identifies more than one recipient. The information or instruction being told can follow after que.

example.es: Quiero decirles que lleguen temprano.
example.en: I want to tell them to arrive early.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; introduces the action someone is told to do
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After decir used to give an instruction, que links the instruction to the person receiving it. Natural English often uses “to” before the action instead of translating que as “that.”

example.es: Le digo que espere.
example.en: I tell her to wait.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks ponerse a, “to start doing”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In ponerse a, the small pronoun changes with the person: me pongo, te pones, se pone, nos ponemos, os ponéis, or se ponen. English normally expresses the full construction as “start” or “get down to.”

example.es: Se pone a limpiar.
example.en: She starts cleaning.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: they start; they get down to it (special form of poner)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pongan is a form of poner for more than one person. It is used here after an instruction rather than as a plain statement; ordinary ponen changes to pongan. With se and a following action, se pongan a means that they start that action.

example.es: Quiero que se pongan a estudiar.
example.en: I want them to start studying.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links ponerse to the action that begins
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ponerse a requires a before the following action verb. English expresses the full construction as “start doing” and does not translate this a separately.

example.es: Nos ponemos a cocinar.
example.en: We start cooking.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to work; to get to work (informal, especially in Spain)
happened; occurred (completed-action form)
no separate English word; article used before a product or software name
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish can put el before the name of software, a vehicle model, or another product when a masculine noun such as sistema or modelo is understood. English often uses the product name without an article.

example.es: Compró el Toyota rojo.
example.en: She bought the red Toyota.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I knew; he, she, or formal you knew; used to know
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sabía is an imperfect past form of saber, “to know.” The imperfect presents knowledge as a state that was already true or ongoing, instead of as a single completed discovery. Context tells whether the subject is I, he, she, or formal you.

example.es: Ella sabía la respuesta.
example.en: She knew the answer.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What does nivel de alcohol en sangre name in a medical or legal measurement?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: It means “blood alcohol concentration”: the amount of alcohol present in the blood.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Nivel names the measured level, de alcohol names the substance, and en sangre says where it is measured. Spanish may abbreviate the term with the initials N.A.S.; English commonly uses B.A.C.

example.es: El médico midió el nivel de alcohol en sangre.
example.en: The doctor measured the blood alcohol concentration.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the comic's fictional narrow blood-alcohol range in which programming ability suddenly peaks
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The name refers to Microsoft executive Steve Ballmer. The joke presents a precise alcohol optimum as if it were a documented scientific effect, then treats Windows ME's poor reputation as evidence of an uncontrolled attempt to exploit it.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens in the late part of a month, year, decade, or other period?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a finales de, followed by the period.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A is fixed in this expression, finales is the plural of final, “end,” and de introduces the period. English commonly says “in late…” or “at the end of…,” depending on context.

example.es: El curso termina a finales de julio.
example.en: The course ends in late July.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens “somehow” or in an unspecified way?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use de alguna manera.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The three words work together as an expression of manner. It can say that the way is unknown, unexplained, or simply not important enough to specify.

example.es: De alguna manera, abrimos la puerta.
example.en: Somehow, we opened the door.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is done “just like that,” without extra thought, preparation, or explanation?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use sin más.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This fixed expression literally suggests “without anything more.” Depending on context, it can mean simply, without further ado, without another word, or with no additional precautions.

example.es: No aceptó la propuesta sin más.
example.en: She did not accept the proposal just like that.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: decirle a alguien que + acción pedida
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you report an instruction by saying that someone tells another person to do something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of decir with the recipient, then que, then a special verb form for the requested action.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The recipient appears as le or les, sometimes attached as in decirle or decirles. After que, Spanish uses the subjunctive, a verb form for a requested action rather than a stated fact. For example, ordinary pone or ponen changes to ponga or pongan. Match that final verb to the person being asked to act.

example.es: La maestra les dice que abran el libro.
example.en: The teacher tells them to open the book.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone starts or gets down to doing an action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching small pronoun and a form of poner, then a, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The small pronoun changes with the person: me pongo, te pones, se pone, nos ponemos, os ponéis, or se ponen. Poner also changes for the person and time. The final action stays in its dictionary form, the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir.

example.es: Después de cenar, nos ponemos a estudiar.
example.en: After dinner, we start studying.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: a Microsoft Windows release widely remembered for instability and other problems
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Windows Millennium Edition appeared in 2000 and developed a poor reputation. Mentioning it as the result of a programming experiment makes the response function as a punchline rather than a neutral product reference.
